title: Questioning the Survey Responses of Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The paper measures the alignment of language model responses with the survey responses of various demographic subgroups, including religious groups. It re-examines a finding from prior work which suggested models were most aligned with Protestant or Roman Catholic groups, and analyzes this alignment through the lens of response entropy.
findings: The paper argues that prior findings showing language models are more 'aligned' with Protestant or Roman Catholic groups are not due to the models representing these groups' values. Instead, this alignment is an artifact of systematic biases. The models tend to produce high-entropy (close to uniform) responses, and these specific religious subgroups happened to have the highest entropy (most balanced) survey answers among the religion demographic subgroups considered. Therefore, the perceived alignment is a proxy for the entropy of the subgroup's responses, not an inherent property of the model.
